text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a p99/p999 tail on ingress that lines up with host preproc work after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Regression only on short payload routes (~<300B).

leo: How big is the regression? numbers?

anya: p99 +22ms, p999 +48ms on canary. CPU for host-ingress unchanged. Flare points to parse/tokenize + small-write path.

anya: perf excerpt:
```
  host_preproc() 82%
    parse_http() 39%
      read_loop() 21%
        small_writev_fastpath() 13%
          tcp_cork_toggle() 6%
        memcpy+alloc 8%
    kv_prefix_lookup() 15%
    route_dispatch() 10%
```

jamal: tcp_cork_toggle? We toggle cork to coalesce then uncork earlier for streaming. Could toggling more often after smaller batches explain the spike?

tara: Related note: kernel-selector started preferring kernel B for short seqs -> we end up with smaller batching windows on those routes. Smaller batches => more frequent flushes.

leo: I instrumented HTTP vs gRPC: gRPC keeps larger frames because of client-side buffering; HTTP endpoints are the ones spiking. So this is ingress framing + batching interplay.

anya: I pushed a quick experiment on canary: enabled delayed-unset of TCP_CORK for 8ms (instead of immediate uncork on first byte). Canary shows p99 -14ms, p999 -30ms, throughput stable. CPU +1.8% on ingress.

infra-bot: deploy started by anya for service/ingress-proxy canary (canary-22).

jamal: Good win, but we still see kv_prefix_lookup allocations up. Any clues?

tara: With smaller batches there's less prefix reuse inside a batch; our kv keys include a batch-id component when batch_size==1 which makes keys uniq. Kernel change increased singletons.

leo: So the chain is: kernel-selector -> smaller batches -> more frequent cork toggles + more unique kv keys -> malloc churn -> tail.

anya: Proposed mitigation plan:
- Keep delayed-unset cork as short-term guard.
- Add a 'batch_coalesce' knob to server config to favor merging tiny requests for routes tagged as short-seq.
- Fix kv key composition: remove batch-id from key when body < 512B (cheap heuristic) to improve prefix reuse.

jamal: Priorities: 1) quick cork delay deploy (done), 2) kv key change (low-risk) + bench, 3) batching knob (needs perf validation).

leo: Also add telemetry: per-route batch_size histogram, cork-toggle rate, kv_hit_rate. That will help us detect regressions before we touch kernel rules.

anya: I'll keep the cork change for 6h observation and open PRs for kv key tweak + batching flag.

infra-bot: deploy succeeded (canary-22) at ts=7329991168

anya: After 2h: p99 down ~12ms, p999 down ~28ms on majority of routes. One route (mobile-client A) shows slight increase in latency variance — investigating.

tara: If mobile-client A breaks, we should consider gate for client-id header so cork logic respects known low-latency clients.

jamal: I'll draft rollback steps for cork toggle and prepare a short-window batching canary config.

anya: Thanks team. Posting perf graphs in #eng-runtime and will follow up with PR links. :rocket:
